newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore groups shun Malaysian holidays - paper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore groups shun Malaysian holidays - paper.

text.p: Singapore community groups linked to the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) are boycotting Malaysia for holidays following tension between Singapore and its northern neighbour, the Sunday Times said.

The newspaper said "grassroots bodies" -- PAP-linked residents committees and local community organisations -- were avoiding Malaysia to show support for Singapore, for Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and also to avoid being attacked.
Relations between Singapore and Malaysia took a dive earlier this year after Lee, Singapore's long-time former prime minister, made disparaging remarks about the southern Malaysian state of Johor.
Lee said in a court affidavit in a libel suit against an opposition politician that Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
The comments provoked intense anger in Kuala Lumpur and a major row which was eventually calmed by a rare, unreserved apology by Lee.

But the Sunday Times said many organisations from the island-state were avoiding trips to Malaysia for the traditional holiday season this June, preferring instead to visit Indonesia and Thailand, which offered cheaper vacations.
"Such tours used to go to Malaysia but not this June," it quoted one unidentified travel agent as saying.
"Although Malaysia is convenient, the groups didn't feel welcome there at this time, and decided to go to other neighbouring countries until the tension wore off," said another.
The newspaper quoted the chairman of one local group as saying it would not be going to Malaysia for the time being.
"We want to show our support for the government," he said.
On an average weekend, about 100,000 Singaporeans cross the traffic-jammed causeway into Malaysia.
Malaysian politicians have criticised the pro-government Singapore press in recent weeks for hostile stories.
Malaysian trade minister Rafidah Aziz called for a "media war" against Singapore after the Singapore daily Straits Times published a report about levels of crime in Johor.
The newspaper said Lee was probably justified in his criticism of Johor as an unsafe place.
The Sunday Times said cost was also a factor weighing against Malaysian holidays this year.
"It's cheaper to travel to Thailand than to Malaysia," it quoted one travel agent as saying.
